description: Sedimentary exhalative (clastic-dominated) zinc-lead: stratiform sulfide in euxinic black shale of a rift or sag basin beside a thick–thin lithosphere step, zoned Cu → Pb → Zn away from its feeder.

driver.note: active rift or sag subsidence with growth faults (design thresholds)
basinal brines heated to 100–200 °C (SIR 2010-5070-N p. 2); thresholds are design

pathway.note: 85 % of sediment-hosted base metals lie within 200 km of a thick–thin lithosphere step (Hoggard et al. 2020); the taper is design

notes: Sizing: USGS OFR 2009-1252 (Singer, Berger & Moring 2009), model SHam (shale-hosted, amagmatic), n = 25, Table 2 p. 10: tonnage 5 / 25 / 300 Mt, Zn 2.3 / 8 / 14 %, Pb 0.88 / 2.1 / 5.3 %, Ag 0 / 21 / 71 g/t, Cu 0 / 0 / 1.0 % (unreported grades counted as zero); Zn–Pb r = 0.72 (text); 2 km same-deposit rule (p. 2). All 25 SHam deposits are labelled SEDEX (they are 25 of the report's 179 SEDEX-labelled deposits). presence = n_reported / 25 from the report's database. Bulletin 1693 model 31a (n = 45) is in data/usgs/sedex_zn_pb.json extra. Au (4 of 25) is left out.

PLACEHOLDERS (not found in any USGS source): ore_density_t_m3 3.2 (sulfide-rich shale), density_per_1e5km2 0.5 / 2 / 8 (no USGS SEDEX deposit density exists), formation_depth_m 100 (syn-sedimentary to early diagenetic).

Geometry: stratiform sheet; aspect 0.03 from the database's median ore area 0.86 km² and ore bodies up to a few tens of metres thick (B1693 m31a); the Cu → Pb → Zn lateral zoning away from the feeder (Leach et al. 2010).
Create stones (decisions file): dolostone (asurine → zinc) is a preferred host at 1.5; the sheet turns its host to black shale.

Counts (survivor formula, decisions log 2026-09-29, plan §8.6 as built): the density counts deposits that survive to the present, as USGS does; the engine forms more (deposits/survival.rs) so that the expected survivors are ρ_p50 · permissive area · count_mult. balance.count_mult stays 1: a pack lever, not a calibration. With the placeholder density the euxinic rift tracts of a 16k planet (6,500–22,000 km²) expect 0.1–0.45 survivors, so SEDEX is on a minority of planets (STATUS.md, 2026-09-29).
